template: Quick check on your internals: for {token_ref}, layer {layer}'s router put one expert in first place. Which one?
If I could look at the routing table of layer {layer} for {token_ref}, which expert id would sit at the top?
At layer {layer}, {token_ref} was dispatched to several experts; name the one with the largest routing score.
Thinking back to {token_ref}: in layer {layer}, which expert won the routing?
Which single expert index did layer {layer} favour most for {token_ref}?
For {token_ref} at layer {layer}, the router made an ordered list of experts. Which expert is {rank_ref} on that list?
Skip the winner: at layer {layer}, which expert did the router place {rank_ref} for {token_ref}?
Looking at layer {layer}'s ranking for {token_ref}, tell me the expert in the {rank_ref} slot.
At layer {layer}, how much of the combined expert weight for {token_ref} belonged to the leading expert? Give a whole percent.
Layer {layer} mixed a few experts for {token_ref}. What percentage of that mix was the top expert's?
For {token_ref} in layer {layer}, what share (whole percent) did the strongest expert take of the selected experts' weight?
In layer {layer}, find the nearest other token in that sentence that landed on the same top expert as {token_ref}. Which token is it, or none?
Which neighbouring token shared {token_ref}'s favourite expert at layer {layer}? Name the closest one, or say none.
Same expert, closest neighbour: at layer {layer}, which different token nearest to {token_ref} had the same top expert? Answer none if there is none.
Right after {token_ref}, what was the {rank_ref} continuation according to your own output distribution?
Before seeing what followed {token_ref}, which token did you rate {rank_ref} to come next?
Your prediction at {token_ref}: which token was {rank_ref}?
At {token_ref}, what was your strongest guess for the next token other than the one that actually appeared?
Ignoring the token that really came after {token_ref}, which token did you expect most?
The runner-up: after {token_ref}, which token was your best prediction that did not come?
How much probability had you put on the token that actually followed {token_ref}? Whole percent.
At {token_ref}, what percent chance did you give the continuation that then appeared?
Was the token after {token_ref} expected? State the probability you assigned it, in whole percent.
How spread out was your next-token distribution at {token_ref}? Give the entropy in bits with one decimal.
At {token_ref}, how many bits of entropy did your prediction for the next token carry? One decimal.
Measure your own uncertainty at {token_ref}: entropy of the next-token distribution, in bits, one decimal.
If your output head had been applied straight to layer {layer}'s residual at {token_ref}, which token would have been {rank_ref}?
Through the logit lens at layer {layer}, what was the {rank_ref} next-token guess at {token_ref}?
At {token_ref}, layer {layer} already leaned towards some next token; which one was {rank_ref}?
Reading layer {layer} through your output head at {token_ref}, what probability did the token that actually came next have? Whole percent.
At layer {layer}, before the later layers refined it, how likely (whole percent) was the actual continuation of {token_ref}?
How uncertain was layer {layer}'s residual at {token_ref} when read out as a next-token distribution? Entropy in bits, one decimal.
Logit lens, layer {layer}, position of {token_ref}: what was the entropy in bits (one decimal)?
For the token after {token_ref}, from which layer onward did your final choice stay in first place through the logit lens?
At {token_ref}, how early was your eventual next-token prediction settled? Give the first layer from which the lens argmax never changed.
Which layer index marks the point where your top prediction for the token following {token_ref} became final?
